description: Threshold sensitivity analysis for CIVO detector magnitude threshold (tau_mag)

non_triggering_negatives.reason: No checkpoint has acceleration=true AND eval_decline_count>=2 simultaneously, regardless of magnitude threshold

conclusion: tau_mag=0.49 is the tightest (most conservative) threshold that achieves maximum Youden's J=0.714. The operating curve has a sharp cliff at tau=0.50 where exp_008d_s3 (ve_ratio=0.4969) drops out, reducing J from 0.714 to 0.381. FPR is invariant across [0.30, 0.70] because both FP cases (exp_009c at 0.7499, exp_009a at 0.7281) have trigger ve_ratios above 0.70. The 2 FPs cannot be eliminated by magnitude threshold alone without also losing 2/3 TPs. Lowering tau below 0.49 gains nothing (no new TPs or FPs). The current threshold 0.49 is optimal: it sits just below the critical ve_ratio of exp_008d_s3 (0.4969), capturing all true positives at minimum false alarm rate achievable within the [0.30, 0.70] range.
insight: The magnitude threshold primarily gates the most marginal TP case (exp_008d_s3). The 2 FP cases have high ve_ratios (0.73, 0.75) and cannot be separated from TPs by magnitude alone. Reducing FPR requires improving other conditions (e.g., temporal persistence, minimum trigger step, or acceleration threshold).
